claims.claim: The prospective authoring policy now requires explicit minimum-sufficient-v1 while retaining both historical policy identities.
V1 retains the existing isolated direct execution path for ordered authored commands, without V2 derivation or implicit additional suites.
V1 retains raw-exit-zero success requirements and blocking failure handling across PRIMARY, REMEDIATION and REPAIR, without baseline attribution waivers.
The prospective ingress gate rejects new V2 authoring; identical historical replay and historical V2 execution, decoding and transport paths remain unchanged.
Focused regression cases cover direct ordering, success and failure, admission policy, historical V2 compatibility, malformed or missing evidence, and exact command/RUN/subject identity.
Both current authoring contracts describe reviewed-publication activation of V1, V2 bootstrap and historical compatibility, and preserved authority boundaries.

The committed implementation changes only the nine permitted files, introduces no Runtime service or authority, and preserves TASK-355 r5, admitted TASK-356, frozen Kernel, KA-01 and historical artifacts. No full suite was executed.
